mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a stable downward drift over the last four weeks (-16.0 to -17.0), reflecting persistent reduced retail activity. This momentum will continue into the next four weeks absent a shock, keeping RETAIL_REC flat-to-lower relative to the prior period.
evidence_refs: fact: RETAIL_REC declined from -16.0 to -17.0 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: If mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days rises more than 2 points above the -17.0 level, reversing the observed downward drift, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A TRANSIT mobility decline crossing -27% signals constrained access to transit-dependent retail districts such as central London, causing RETAIL_REC to fall further over the following two weeks as fewer shoppers reach retail hubs via public transport.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -27 points for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact: TRANSIT declined from -25.1 to -27.6 over the last four weeks, crossing -27 in the most recent week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline, or instead rises, in the two weeks following a TRANSIT reading below -27, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicate reduced weekday commuting and the loss of associated lunchtime and after-work retail visits. Their joint negative trend compounds to suppress RETAIL_REC more than either series alone would predict over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both decline week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES moved from -9.9 to -10.3 and TRANSIT from -25.1 to -27.6 concurrently over the last four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks despite continued joint decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: As London enters early spring (mid-March), rising daylight hours and improving weather typically reverse recent PARKS mobility declines, and outdoor-linked footfall spillover increases visits to nearby retail and recreation sites, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS fell from -12.4 to -20.9 before partially stabilizing at -19.1, suggesting a trough near the seasonal transition point
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to decline below -20 and RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next four weeks, the seasonal rebound hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive weekly decline in GROCERY_PHARM (from -0.3 to -2.9) signals growing caution or reduced non-essential errand bundling, which precedes a short-term dip in RETAIL_REC within one week as shoppers consolidate and reduce discretionary trips.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM declines for three consecutive weeks by more than 1 point cumulative
evidence_refs: fact: GROCERY_PHARM fell monotonically from -0.3 to -2.9 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC increases in the week immediately following a three-week GROCERY_PHARM decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has plateaued within a narrow band (-9.6 to -10.3) over the last four weeks, indicating a stabilized hybrid-work policy environment. Because this plateau removes the commuting-driven lift seen in office-dependent retail footfall, RETAIL_REC will remain stagnant or drift lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES ranged narrowly between -9.6 and -10.3 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises by more than 2 points over the next four weeks while WORKPLACES remains within the same plateau band, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has remained persistently elevated (13.9-14.7%) over the last four weeks, indicating sustained home-centric behavior. This persistent elevation signals continued reduced out-of-home discretionary trips, which will keep RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL stayed within a 13.9-14.7 range over the last four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks while RESIDENTIAL remains at or above 13.9, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in PARKS and TRANSIT indicate a broad contraction of out-of-home mobility across both leisure and transit-dependent trip types. Their combined negative momentum amplifies downward pressure on RETAIL_REC beyond what either factor alone would produce, over a two-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and TRANSIT both decline week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS fell from -12.4 to -20.9 and TRANSIT fell from -25.1 to -27.6 concurrently over the last four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next two weeks despite continued joint decline in PARKS and TRANSIT, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.
